California Licensed Physical Therapy Assistant

Minimum education satisfied through attainment of the required licensure/certification
2 years of clinical experience as a Licensed Physical Therapist Assistant

The Physical Therapist Assistant (PTA) is an integral member of the Physical Medicine and Rehabilitation (PM&R) team, providing skilled, evidence-based treatment under the general supervision of a licensed Physical Therapist. Working collaboratively with Physical Therapists, and other healthcare professionals, the PTA helps patients regain mobility, maximize function, and achieve their rehabilitation goals through compassionate, patient-centered care.
80% - Provides patient treatment and patient care activities for routine and more difficult, complicated paitients as directed by a therapist form predetermined physical therapy treatment plan.

This position is ideal for an experienced PTA who enjoys clinical variety and professional growth. The PTA delivers care across multiple practice settings, including acute care, and outpatient services, with opportunities to expand clinical expertise while working with diverse patient populations. The successful candidate demonstrates strong clinical judgment, adaptability, excellent communication skills, and a commitment to delivering exceptional patient outcomes in a collaborative academic medical center.
